title.zh: 卷六十一 列傳第五十一 陳伯之 陳慶之 蘭欽
title.en: Volume 61 Biographies 51: Chen Bozhi, Chen Qingzhi, Lan Qin
title.raw: 卷六十一 列傳第五十一 陳伯之 陳慶之 蘭欽 Volume 61 Biographies 51: Chen Bozhi, Chen Qingzhi, Lan Qin

sentences.zh: 陳伯之

translations.literal: Chen Bozhi
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bozhi

sentences.zh: 陳伯之，濟陰睢陵人也。

translations.literal: Chen Bozhi was a native of Suiling in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bozhi was from Suiling in Jiyin commandery.

sentences.zh: 年十三四，好著獺皮冠，帶刺刀，候鄰里稻熟，輒偷刈之。

translations.literal: At the age of thirteen or fourteen, he liked to wear an otter-skin cap and carry a dagger; when the rice in neighboring fields ripened, he would steal and reap it.
translations.idiomatic: When he was thirteen or fourteen, he favored an otter-skin cap and a dagger at his side. He would watch the neighbors' rice ripen and then sneak in to cut it.

sentences.zh: 嘗為田主所見，呵之曰：「楚子莫動！」

translations.literal: Once he was seen by the field owner, who shouted at him: "You Chu lad, don't move!
translations.idiomatic: Once the field's owner caught him and shouted, "You scoundrel—hold still!

sentences.zh: 伯之曰：「君稻幸多，取一擔何苦。」

translations.literal: Bozhi said: "Your rice happens to be plentiful; what harm is there in taking a single load?"
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi replied, "You've got plenty of grain—what's one load between us?"

sentences.zh: 田主將執之。

translations.literal: The field owner was about to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: The owner moved to seize him.

sentences.zh: 因拔刀而進，曰：「楚子定何如！」

translations.literal: Thereupon he drew his knife and advanced, saying: "Well, Chu lad, what now!
translations.idiomatic: He whipped out his knife and stepped forward. "Well now—what are you going to do about it?

sentences.zh: 田主皆反走，徐擔稻而歸。

translations.literal: The field owner and his companions all turned and fled; he slowly shouldered the rice and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The owner and his men fled. Bozhi calmly loaded up the rice and went home.

sentences.zh: 及年長，在鍾離數為劫盜，嘗授面覘人船，船人斫之，獲其左耳。

translations.literal: When he grew older, at Zhongli he repeatedly engaged in robbery and pillage; once he covered his face and spied on a boat, and the boatmen hacked at him, taking his left ear.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he turned to brigandage around Zhongli. Once, with his face disguised, he was scouting a boat when the crew struck at him and sliced off his left ear.

sentences.zh: 後隨鄉人車騎將軍王廣之，廣之愛其勇，每夜臥下榻，征伐常將自隨。

translations.literal: Later he followed his fellow townsman the Cavalry General Wang Guangzhi; Guangzhi admired his courage, had him sleep on the lower couch every night, and on campaigns always kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: He later attached himself to Wang Guangzhi, Cavalry General and a fellow native of his district. Wang favored his daring, had him sleep on the lower bunk each night, and kept him close on every campaign.

sentences.zh: 頻以戰功，累遷驃騎司馬，封魚復縣伯。

translations.literal: Through repeated military achievements, he was promoted step by step to Biaoqi Commandant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yufu county.
translations.idiomatic: Battle honors piled up until he rose to Biaoqi Commandant and was enfeoffed as Count of Yufu.

sentences.zh: 梁武起兵，東昏假伯之節，督前驅諸軍事、豫州刺史，轉江州，據尋陽以拒梁武。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised his army, Dong Hun bestowed upon Bozhi the imperial tally, appointing him to command the vanguard armies as Inspector of Yuzhou; he was transferred to Jiangzhou and held Xunyang to resist Emperor Wu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang took up arms, Dong Hun gave Bozhi imperial authority, made him commander of the advance forces and Inspector of Yuzhou, then moved him to Jiangzhou to hold Xunyang against the Liang founder.

sentences.zh: 郢城平，武帝使說伯之，即以為江州刺史。

translations.literal: When Ying city was pacified, Emperor Wu sent envoys to persuade Bozhi, and immediately appointed him Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Ying fell, Emperor Wu sent men to win him over and at once named him Inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子武牙為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Wuya was made Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wuya was appointed Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 伯之雖受命，猶懷兩端。

translations.literal: Although Bozhi accepted the appointment, he still wavered between two sides.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi took the commission but remained of two minds.

sentences.zh: 帝及其猶豫逼之，伯之退保南湖，然後歸附，與眾軍俱下。

translations.literal: The Emperor, aware of his hesitation, pressed him; Bozhi withdrew to defend South Lake, then submitted, and descended with the other armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, reading his wavering, pressed him hard. Bozhi fell back to South Lake before finally submitting and marching south with the rest of the army.

sentences.zh: 建康城未平，每降人出，伯之輒喚與耳語。

translations.literal: Before Jiankang was pacified, whenever a defector came out, Bozhi would call him over and speak in his ear.
translations.idiomatic: While Jiankang still held out, every time a defector emerged Bozhi would pull him aside for a whispered word.

sentences.zh: 帝疑其復懷翻覆，會東昏將鄭伯倫降，帝使過伯之，謂曰：「城中甚忿卿，欲遣信誘卿，須卿降，當生割卿手腳。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspected he again harbored treacherous intent. It happened that Zheng Bolun, a general of Dong Hun, surrendered; the Emperor sent him to visit Bozhi, saying: "Those in the city are very angry with you; they intend to send someone to lure you over, and once you surrender they will flay your hands and feet while you live.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor suspected another reversal. When Dong Hun's general Zheng Bolun surrendered, he sent him to Bozhi with this message: "The city is furious with you. They plan to lure you in—and once you defect, they'll cut off your hands and feet alive.

sentences.zh: 卿若不降，復欲遣刺客殺卿。」

translations.literal: If you do not surrender, they again intend to send assassins to kill you.
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse, they'll send assassins after you instead.

sentences.zh: 伯之大懼，自是無異志矣。

translations.literal: Bozhi was greatly afraid, and from then on had no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi was terrified. From that moment his loyalty held.

sentences.zh: 城平，封豐城縣公，遣之鎮。

translations.literal: When the city was pacified, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Fengcheng county and dispatched to his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, he was made Duke of Fengcheng and sent to take up his post.

sentences.zh: 伯之不識書，及還江州，得文牒辭訟，唯作大諾而已。

translations.literal: Bozhi could not read; when he returned to Jiangzhou and received written documents and lawsuits, he could only shout "Yes!" in response.
translations.idiomatic: Illiterate, Bozhi returned to Jiangzhou and could do no more than bark assent when documents and lawsuits were read aloud.

sentences.zh: 有事，典簽傳口語，與奪決於主者。

translations.literal: When there was business, the registrar relayed oral instructions, and decisions to grant or withhold rested with the chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Business passed through the registrar by word of mouth; the chief clerk decided everything.

sentences.zh: 伯之子武牙時為直合將軍，武帝手疏龍符罪親付武牙，武牙封示伯之。

translations.literal: Bozhi's son Wuya was then Direct Gate General; Emperor Wu personally wrote out Long Fu's crimes on a sealed document and entrusted it to Wuya, who opened and showed it to Bozhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wuya was Direct Gate General. The Emperor wrote out Long Fu's crimes by hand, sealed the note, and sent it to Wuya, who opened it and showed his father.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣代江州別駕鄧繕，伯之並不受命，曰：「龍符健兒，鄧繕在事有績。

translations.literal: The Emperor also sent someone to replace Jiangzhou's acting administrator Deng Shan; Bozhi refused both orders, saying: "Long Fu is a stalwart man, and Deng Shan has a record of achievement in office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also tried to replace Jiangzhou's vice-governor Deng Shan. Bozhi refused both appointments. "Long Fu is a solid man," he said, "and Deng Shan has served well.

sentences.zh: 台所遣別駕，請以為中從事。」

translations.literal: The acting administrator dispatched by the capital—please appoint him instead as Central Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: As for the vice-governor the court wants to send—keep him on as Central Assistant instead.

sentences.zh: 繕於是日夜說伯之云：「台家府庫空竭，無復器仗，三倉無米。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shan day and night urged Bozhi, saying: "The court's treasuries are empty and drained; there are no more weapons, and the three granaries have no rice.
translations.idiomatic: Shan then worked on Bozhi night and day. "The court's coffers are bare," he said. "There are no arms left, and the granaries are empty.

sentences.zh: 此萬世一時，機不可失。」

translations.literal: This is a once-in-ten-thousand-generations moment; the opportunity must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: This is a chance that comes once in an age—you can't let it slip."

sentences.zh: 緭、承忠等每贊成之。

translations.literal: Chi, Cheng Zhong, and the others constantly seconded this view.
translations.idiomatic: Chi and Cheng Zhong kept urging him on.

sentences.zh: 伯之謂繕：「今段啟卿，若復不得，便與卿共下。」

translations.literal: Bozhi said to Shan: "This time I shall memorialize on your behalf; if I again fail to obtain approval, I will go downriver with you together.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi told Shan, "I'll petition for you this round. If the court refuses again, I'll rebel alongside you.

sentences.zh: 使反，武帝敕部內一郡處繕。

translations.literal: When he rebelled, Emperor Wu ordered one commandery within the province to take Shan in.
translations.idiomatic: When Bozhi did rebel, the Emperor ordered a commandery in the province to accept Shan.

sentences.zh: 伯之於是集府州佐史，謂曰：「奉齊建安王教，率江北義勇十萬已次六合，見使以江州見力運糧速下。

translations.literal: Bozhi thereupon assembled the provincial and prefectural clerks and said: "By order of the Prince of Jian'an of Qi, I lead a hundred thousand righteous volunteers from north of the Yangtze who have already camped at Luhe; I am ordered to use Jiangzhou's existing forces to transport grain and descend swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi gathered his staff and announced: "By command of Qi's Prince of Jian'an, a hundred thousand volunteers from north of the Yangtze are encamped at Luhe. I am to mobilize Jiangzhou's forces, move grain, and march south at once.

sentences.zh: 我荷明帝厚恩，誓以死報。」

translations.literal: I have received the thick grace of Emperor Ming and swear to repay it with my death.
translations.idiomatic: I owe Emperor Ming a great debt and swear to repay it with my life.

sentences.zh: 使緭詐為蕭寶寅書以示僚佐，於聽事前為壇，殺牲以盟。

translations.literal: He had Chi forge a letter from Xiao Baoyin to show the officials; before the reception hall they set up an altar and slaughtered a beast to swear alliance.
translations.idiomatic: He had Chi forge a letter from Xiao Baoyin for the staff. Before the hall they erected an altar and cut throats to seal the oath.

sentences.zh: 伯之先歃，長史以下次第歃。

translations.literal: Bozhi drank the blood-oath first; from the chief administrator downward they drank in order.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi swore first; the chief administrator and all ranks below followed in turn.

sentences.zh: 緭說伯之：「今舉大事，宜引人望。

translations.literal: Chi urged Bozhi: "In undertaking this great matter, you should bring in men of reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Chi advised him: "For an undertaking this large, you need men of standing.

sentences.zh: 程元沖不與人同心；

translations.literal: Cheng Yuanchong does not share the same mind as others;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanchong is not with us;

sentences.zh: 臨川內史王觀，僧虔之孫，人身不惡，可召為長史，以代元沖。」

translations.literal: Wang Guan, Administrator of Linchuan and grandson of Sengqian—his person is not disagreeable—may be summoned as chief administrator to replace Yuanchong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guan, Administrator of Linchuan and grandson of Wang Sengqian, is well regarded. Summon him as chief administrator to replace Yuanchong.

sentences.zh: 伯之從之，仍以緭為尋陽太守，承忠輔義將軍，龍符豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Bozhi complied; he moreover appointed Chi as Administrator of Xunyang, Cheng Zhong as Assistant Righteous General, and Long Fu as Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi agreed. He made Chi prefect of Xunyang, Cheng Zhong an Assistant Righteous General, and Long Fu Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 豫章太守鄭伯倫起郡兵拒守。

translations.literal: Zheng Bolun, Administrator of Yuzhang, raised the commandery troops to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Bolun, prefect of Yuzhang, mustered the commandery troops and held out.

sentences.zh: 程元沖既失職，於家合率數百人，使伯之典簽呂孝通、戴元則為內應。

translations.literal: Cheng Yuanchong, having lost his office, at home gathered several hundred men and had Bozhi's registrars Lu Xiaotong and Dai Yuanze serve as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of his post, Yuanchong rallied several hundred men at home and enlisted Bozhi's registrars Lu Xiaotong and Dai Yuanze as inside agents.

sentences.zh: 伯之每旦常作伎，日晡輒臥，左右仗身皆休息。

translations.literal: Bozhi every morning usually enjoyed performances; when the sun slanted west he would lie down, and the armed attendants on his left and right all rested.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning Bozhi watched entertainments; by afternoon he napped, and his armed guards rested too.

sentences.zh: 元沖因其解弛，從北門入，徑至聽事前。

translations.literal: Yuanchong, taking advantage of this relaxation, entered from the north gate and went straight to the reception hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchong exploited the lull, came in through the north gate, and marched straight to the hall.

sentences.zh: 伯之聞叫，自率出蕩。

translations.literal: Bozhi heard the shouting and personally led men out to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the uproar, Bozhi rushed out at the head of his men.

sentences.zh: 元衝力不能敵，走逃廬山。

translations.literal: Yuanchong's strength was insufficient to resist; he fled to Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Outmatched, Yuanchong fled to Mount Lu.

sentences.zh: 伯之遣使還報武牙兄弟，武牙等走盱眙，盱眙人徐文安、莊興紹、張顯明邀擊之，不能禁，反見殺。

translations.literal: Bozhi sent envoys back to report to Wuya and his brothers; Wuya and the others fled to Xuyi. Xu Wen'an, Zhuang Xingshao, and Zhang Xianming of Xuyi intercepted them but could not stop them and were themselves killed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi sent word to Wuya and his brothers. They fled toward Xuyi, where local men Xu Wen'an, Zhuang Xingshao, and Zhang Xianming tried to stop them—failed—and were killed instead.

sentences.zh: 武帝遣王茂討伯之，敗走，間道亡命出江北，與子武牙及褚緭俱入魏。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu dispatched Wang Mao to attack Bozhi; Bozhi was defeated and fled, escaping by hidden paths north of the Yangtze; together with his son Wuya and Chu Chi he entered Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sent Wang Mao against him. Defeated, Bozhi slipped out by back roads north of the Yangtze and fled to Wei with Wuya and Chu Chi.

sentences.zh: 魏以伯之為使持節、散騎常侍、都督淮南諸軍事、平南將軍、光祿大夫、曲江縣侯。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Bozhi as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of all Huainan military affairs, General Who Pacifies the South, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Marquis of Qujiang county.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made him Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, commander of Huainan forces, General Who Pacifies the South, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Marquis of Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 天監四年，詔太尉臨川王巨集北侵，巨集命記室丘遲私與之書曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian, an edict ordered the Grand Marshal the Prince of Linchuan Hunchu to invade the north; Hunchu ordered his secretary Qiu Chi privately to write him a letter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianjian, the Grand Marshal, the Prince of Linchuan, was ordered north. He had his secretary Qiu Chi write Bozhi a private letter:

sentences.zh: 陳將軍足下，無恙，幸甚，幸甚。

translations.literal: To General Chen, at your feet—are you well? How fortunate, how fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: General Chen—I trust you are well. This is a fortunate occasion indeed.

sentences.zh: 將軍勇冠三軍，才為世出。

translations.literal: General, your courage crowns the three armies; your talent exceeds this generation.
translations.idiomatic: Your courage heads the three armies; your talent is unmatched in our age.

sentences.zh: 棄燕雀之毛羽，慕鴻鵠以高翔。

translations.literal: You abandoned the feathers of the sparrow and finch, and admired the wild swan to soar high.
translations.idiomatic: You left behind the petty sparrow and aspired to the wild swan's high flight.

sentences.zh: 昔因機變化，遭遇時主，立功立事，開國稱孤，朱輪華轂，擁旄萬里，何其壯也！

translations.literal: Formerly, seizing opportune change and encountering the sovereign of the age, you achieved merit and established affairs, founding a state and styling yourself a regional lord, with vermilion wheels and ornate axles, holding the banner of command for ten thousand li—how magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Once you seized your moment, found a ruler who valued you, won glory in battle, founded a fief, and rode in vermilion-wheeled carriages bearing command over a thousand miles—how splendid that was!

sentences.zh: 如何一旦為奔亡之虜，聞鳴鏑而股戰，對穹廬以屈膝，又何劣邪？

translations.literal: How is it that in a single day you became a captive fleeing in defeat, trembling in your thighs at the sound of whistling arrows, kneeling before domed tents—how inferior!
translations.idiomatic: Yet in a moment you became a fugitive in enemy hands, shaking at the whistle of arrows, kneeling before nomad tents—how far you have fallen!

sentences.zh: 尋君去就之際，非有他故，直以不能內審諸己，外受流言，沈迷猖蹶，以至於此。

translations.literal: Reflecting on the moment of your going or staying, there was no other cause: simply that you could not examine yourself inwardly and outwardly accepted slanderous rumors, sinking in delusion and recklessness until you came to this.
translations.idiomatic: As I consider your choice to leave, there is no deeper mystery: you failed to look inward, listened to rumor, and stumbled blind into ruin.

sentences.zh: 聖朝赦罪責功，棄瑕錄用，推赤心于天下，安反側於萬物，此將軍之所知，非假僕一二談也。

translations.literal: The sacred court pardons crimes and rewards merit, discarding flaws to employ men, extending its red heart to the world and settling those who turned against it among all things—this the general knows; it needs no word or two from me.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty pardons past wrongs and honors merit, overlooks flaws, and welcomes those who return. Its good faith extends to all the realm. You know this well—I need not rehearse it.

sentences.zh: 昔朱鮪涉血于友于，張繡倳刃於愛子，漢主不以為疑，魏君待之若舊。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhu Wei waded in blood against his friend and younger brother; Zhang Xiu raised the blade against his beloved son; the Han sovereign held no suspicion, and the Wei lord treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wei once washed his hands in a brother's blood; Zhang Xiu turned his blade on a beloved son—and yet the Han emperor did not doubt them, and Wei received Zhang as before.

sentences.zh: 況將軍無昔人之罪，而勳重於當代。

translations.literal: Moreover, the general has not the crimes of those ancients, while his merit outweighs those of the present age.
translations.idiomatic: You have committed no such crime, and your service to the realm weighs heavier still.

sentences.zh: 夫迷塗知反，往哲是與，不遠而復，先典攸高。

translations.literal: To err on the road yet know to return—the sages of old approved this; to turn back without going far—the former classics hold this supreme.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients praised those who lost their way yet knew to turn back; the classics honor the swift return.

sentences.zh: 主上屈法申恩，吞舟是漏。

translations.literal: Our lord bends the law to extend grace; even fish that could swallow a boat are spared the net.
translations.idiomatic: The throne bends the law to show mercy—even great fish escape the net.

sentences.zh: 將軍松柏不翦，親戚安居；

translations.literal: General, your pines and cypresses are uncut, your kinsmen dwell in peace;
translations.idiomatic: Your ancestral graves stand untouched; your kin live untroubled;

sentences.zh: 高堂未傾，愛妾尚在。

translations.literal: Your high hall has not fallen, your beloved concubine still lives.
translations.idiomatic: Your home still stands, your beloved wife still waits.

sentences.zh: 悠悠爾心，亦何可言。

translations.literal: Vast and distant is your heart—what more can be said?
translations.idiomatic: What runs through your mind—is there anything left to say?

sentences.zh: 當今功臣名將，雁行有序，佩紫懷黃，贊帷幄之謀；

translations.literal: The meritorious ministers and famous generals of today, arrayed like wild geese in order, wearing purple sashes and bearing golden seals, assist in the stratagems within the tent curtain;
translations.idiomatic: Today's heroes march in ordered ranks, purple sashes and golden seals at their belts, advising strategy in the command tent;

sentences.zh: 乘軺建節，奉疆埸之任。

translations.literal: Riding light carriages and bearing imperial credentials, they undertake the duties of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing imperial authority on light carriages, they guard the borders.

sentences.zh: 並刑馬作誓，傳之子孫。

translations.literal: All slaughter horses to make oaths and pass these honors to sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: They swear oaths over slaughtered horses and bequeath honor to their heirs.

sentences.zh: 將軍獨靦顏借命，驅馳氈裘之長，寧不哀哉！

translations.literal: General alone, shame-faced, clinging to life, you gallop in service to the chiefs in felt and fur—how is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you alone cling to life in shame, driving horses for fur-clad chieftains—does that not wring the heart?

sentences.zh: 夫以慕容超之強，身送東市，姚泓之盛，面縛西都。

translations.literal: Consider: with Murong Chao's strength, he was sent personally to the eastern market; with Yao Hong's flourishing power, he was bound facing the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao's might could not save him from the execution ground; Yao Hong's splendor ended as a captive in the western capital.

sentences.zh: 故知霜露所均，不育異類，姬漢舊邦，無取雜種。

translations.literal: Thus we know that where frost and dew fall equally, no alien species are nourished; the old territories of Ji and Han have no use for mongrel breeds.
translations.idiomatic: Where frost and dew fall alike, foreign stock does not thrive; the old realm of Huaxia has no place for barbarian blood.

sentences.zh: 北虜僭號中原，多歷年所，惡積禍盈，理至焦爛。

translations.literal: The northern barbarians have arrogated the title in the Central Plain for many years; their wickedness accumulates and calamities overflow—it is logical they should be burnt to ashes.
translations.idiomatic: The northern invaders have usurped the Central Plain for years; wickedness piled high must end in ruin.

sentences.zh: 況偽孽昏狡，自相夷戮，部落攜離，酋豪猜貳。

translations.literal: Moreover, the false heir is dim-witted and cunning, slaughtering one another; tribes scatter and separate, chieftains suspect and divide.
translations.idiomatic: Their pretender is dull and treacherous; they slaughter one another; tribes splinter; chiefs plot against each other.

sentences.zh: 方當系頸蠻邸，縣首藳街。

translations.literal: Soon they will be bound by the neck in the barbarian lodge, their heads displayed on the reed-pole street.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they will be trussed at the barbarian court, heads hung along Reed Street.

sentences.zh: 而將軍魚游于沸鼎之中，燕巢於飛幕之上，不亦惑乎！

translations.literal: Yet the general swims like a fish in a boiling cauldron, nests like a swallow on a flapping tent—are you not confused!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you swim in a boiling pot and nest on a swaying tent—is that not folly?

sentences.zh: 暮春三月，江南草長，雜花生樹，群鸚亂飛。

translations.literal: At the end of spring, in the third month, grasses grow long in Jiangnan; mixed flowers bloom on trees, flocks of parrots fly in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In late spring, when Jiangnan's grass runs long and flowers speckle the trees, when parrots wheel in flocks—

sentences.zh: 見故國之旗鼓，感生平於疇日，撫弦登陴，豈不愴恨。

translations.literal: Seeing the flags and drums of the old country, stirred by one's former life in days past, strumming the lute and mounting the ramparts—would this not be painful regret?
translations.idiomatic: At sight of your homeland's banners, memory of days gone by, the lute in hand atop the wall—would you not ache with regret?

sentences.zh: 所以廉公之思趙將，吳子之泣西河，人之情也，將軍獨無情哉？

translations.literal: This is why Lord Lian thought of the Zhao general, why Master Wu wept for Xihe—it is human feeling; is the general alone without feeling?
translations.idiomatic: Lian Po yearned for Zhao's general; Wu Qi wept for the River West—such is human nature. Have you no heart at all?

sentences.zh: 想早勵良規，自求多福。

translations.literal: I trust you will early encourage good plans and seek much fortune for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to choose wisely, and secure your own blessing.

sentences.zh: 當今皇帝盛明，天下安樂，白環西獻，楛矢東來，夜郎、滇池解辮請職，朝鮮、昌海蹶角受化；

translations.literal: The present emperor is brilliant and enlightened; the realm is at peace and joy; the white ring is offered from the west, hardwood arrows come from the east; Yelang and Dianchi unbind their braids and request office; Chaoxian and Changhai lower their horns and receive transformation;
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor's radiance fills the realm. Tributes stream from every quarter—the white jade ring from the west, hardwood arrows from the east; Yelang and Lake Dian submit; Korea and Changhai bow their horns in obedience.

sentences.zh: 唯北狄野心，掘強沙塞之間，欲延歲月之命耳。

translations.literal: Only the northern Di harbor a wolf's heart, stubborn between sand and frontier fortresses, wishing merely to prolong their days.
translations.idiomatic: Only the northern barbarians, obstinate in the desert passes, cling to a few borrowed years.

sentences.zh: 中軍臨川殿下，明德茂親，總茲戎重，方吊人洛汭，伐罪秦中，若遂不改，方思僕言。

translations.literal: His Highness the Prince of Linchuan, Central Army, of bright virtue and flourishing kinship, holds overall command of these military affairs; presently he consoles the people at Luorui and punishes crime in Qinzhong—if you persist unchanged, then you will recall my words.
translations.idiomatic: His Highness the Prince of Linchuan—virtuous, royal, commander of this campaign—now brings justice to the Luo River and chastisement to Qin. If you refuse to repent, you will soon wish you had heeded me.

sentences.zh: 聊布往懷，君其詳之。

translations.literal: I briefly lay out my past thoughts; may you examine them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: I offer these heartfelt words for your careful reading.

sentences.zh: 伯之得書，乃于壽陽擁眾八千歸降。

translations.literal: Bozhi received the letter and thereupon at Shouyang led eight thousand men to surrender and return.
translations.idiomatic: On receiving the letter, Bozhi rallied eight thousand men at Shouyang and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 武牙為魏人所殺。

translations.literal: Wuya was killed by men of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wuya was killed by the Wei.

sentences.zh: 伯之既至，以為平北將軍、西豫州刺史、永新縣侯。

translations.literal: When Bozhi arrived, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Western Yuzhou, and Marquis of Yongxin county.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his return he was made General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Western Yuzhou, and Marquis of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 未之任。

translations.literal: He did not take up the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 復為驍騎將軍，又為太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was again made General of the Valiant Cavalry and also made Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made General of the Valiant Cavalry and then Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒於家。

translations.literal: After a long time, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In time he died at home.

sentences.zh: 其子猶有在魏者。

translations.literal: Among his sons, some still remained in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his sons remained in Wei.

sentences.zh: 褚緭在魏，魏人欲用之。

translations.literal: Chu Chi was in Wei; the people of Wei wished to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Chi stayed in Wei, where they wished to use him.

sentences.zh: 魏元會，緭戲為詩曰：「帽上著籠冠，緭上著朱衣，不知是今是，不知非昔非。」

translations.literal: At the Wei New Year's assembly, Chi jestingly composed a poem saying: "On the hat one wears a caged crown, on Chi one wears vermilion robes; I know not whether now is now, I know not whether not-the-past is not-the-past.
translations.idiomatic: At the Wei court New Year's gathering, Chi penned a mocking verse: "A caged crown atop the hat, vermilion robes on Chi—who knows if this is now or then, if past and present aren't the same?

sentences.zh: 魏人怒，出為始平太守。

translations.literal: The people of Wei were angered and sent him out as Administrator of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court, furious, sent him out as prefect of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 日日行獵，墮馬而死。

translations.literal: Day after day he went hunting, fell from his horse and died.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted every day until a fall from his horse killed him.

sentences.zh: 陳慶之

translations.literal: Chen Qingzhi
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingzhi

sentences.zh: 陳慶之字子雲，義興國山人也。

translations.literal: Chen Qingzhi, styled Ziyun, was a native of Guoshan in Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingzhi, courtesy name Ziyun, was from Guoshan in Yixing.

sentences.zh: 幼隨從梁武帝。

translations.literal: In youth he followed and attended Emperor Wu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he served Emperor Wu of Liang.

sentences.zh: 帝性好碁，每從夜至旦不輟，等輩皆寐，唯慶之不寢，聞呼即至，甚見親賞。

translations.literal: The Emperor by nature loved weiqi; each session ran from night to dawn without cease; his companions all slept, but Qingzhi alone did not sleep, and at a call he would come at once—he was greatly favored and prized.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor loved weiqi and often played from night until dawn. His companions slept; only Qingzhi stayed awake and answered every summons. The Emperor came to favor him greatly.

sentences.zh: 從平建鄴，稍為主書，散財聚士，恒思立效。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified he followed; he gradually became Master of Writing, dispersed wealth to gather knights, and constantly thought to establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiankang fell he rose to Master of Writing, spent his wealth gathering fighting men, and always looked for a chance to serve.

sentences.zh: 除奉朝請。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 普通中，魏徐州刺史元法僧于彭城求入內附，以慶之為武威將軍，與胡龍牙、成景雋率諸軍應接。

translations.literal: In the Putong era, Yuan Faseng, Inspector of Xuzhou in Wei, at Pengcheng sought to enter and submit; Qingzhi was made General of Martial Prestige and, with Hu Longya and Cheng Jingjun, led the armies to receive and support him.
translations.idiomatic: During Putong, Yuan Faseng, Wei's Inspector of Xuzhou, sought to defect at Pengcheng. Qingzhi was named General of Martial Prestige and, with Hu Longya and Cheng Jingjun, led troops to meet him.

sentences.zh: 還除宣猛將軍、文德主帥，仍率軍送豫章王綜入鎮徐州。

translations.literal: Upon return he was appointed General of Manifest Ferocity and Commander of Wende, and still led the army to escort the Prince of Yuzhang Zong to enter and garrison Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made General of Manifest Ferocity and Commander of Wende, and escorted Prince Zong of Yuzhang to his post at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏遣安豐王元延明、臨淮王元彧率眾十萬來拒。

translations.literal: Wei sent the Prince of Anfeng Yuan Yanming and the Prince of Huaihai Yuan Yu leading an army of one hundred thousand to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent the Princes of Anfeng and Huaihai, Yuan Yanming and Yuan Yu, with a hundred thousand men to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 延明先遣其別將丘大千觀兵近境，慶之擊破之。

translations.literal: Yanming first sent his deputy general Qiu Daqian to observe troops near the border; Qingzhi attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanming first sent his deputy Qiu Daqian to scout the frontier. Qingzhi routed him.

sentences.zh: 後豫章王棄軍奔魏，慶之乃斬關夜退，軍士獲全。

translations.literal: Later the Prince of Yuzhang abandoned the army and fled to Wei; Qingzhi thereupon broke through the pass and retreated by night, and the soldiers were preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zong of Yuzhang abandoned the army and fled to Wei, Qingzhi broke through the pass under cover of night and brought his men out safely.

sentences.zh: 普通七年，安西將軍元樹出征壽春，除慶之假節、總知軍事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Putong, the Anxi General Yuan Shu set out on campaign against Shouchun; Qingzhi was appointed Acting Bearer of the Staff and given overall military command.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Putong, when the Anxi General Yuan Shu marched on Shouchun, Qingzhi was made Acting Bearer of the Staff with overall command.

sentences.zh: 魏豫州刺史李憲遣其子長鈞別築兩城相拒，慶之攻拔之，憲力屈遂降，慶之入據其城。

translations.literal: Li Xian, Inspector of Yuzhou in Wei, sent his son Changjun to build two separate cities to resist; Qingzhi captured them; Xian's strength failed and he surrendered; Qingzhi entered and occupied the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Inspector of Yuzhou Li Xian had his son Changjun build two fortified towns to resist. Qingzhi took both. Li Xian's strength gave out and he surrendered; Qingzhi occupied the city.

sentences.zh: 轉東宮直合。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Direct Gate of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Eastern Palace's Direct Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 大通元年，隸領軍曹仲宗伐渦陽，魏遣常山王元昭等來援，前軍至駝澗，去渦陽四十里。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong, he served under the Commander Cao Congzong to attack Guoyang; Wei sent the Prince of Changshan Yuan Zhao and others to relieve the city; the vanguard reached Tuo Stream, forty li from Guoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong, under Commander Cao Congzong he attacked Guoyang. Wei sent the Prince of Changshan, Yuan Zhao, and others to relieve it. Their vanguard reached Tuo Stream, forty li away.

sentences.zh: 韋放曰：「賊鋒必是輕銳，戰捷不足為功；

translations.literal: Wei Fang said: "The enemy vanguard must be elite troops; victory would not amount to much merit;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fang argued, "The enemy vanguard must be their best troops. Beating them would mean little;

sentences.zh: 如不利，沮我軍勢，不如勿擊。」

translations.literal: If we are defeated, it will dampen our army's momentum—it is better not to fight.
translations.idiomatic: and if we lose, it will break our momentum. Better not engage.

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「魏人遠來，皆已疲倦，須挫其氣，必無不敗之理。」

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "The Wei men come from afar and are all exhausted; we must break their spirit—there is surely no possibility of defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi replied, "The Wei have marched far and are exhausted. We must break their spirit—defeat is certain."

sentences.zh: 於是與麾下五百騎奔擊，破其前軍，魏人震恐。

translations.literal: Thereupon with five hundred cavalry under his command he charged and broke their vanguard; the Wei men were shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: He led five hundred horsemen in a headlong charge, smashed the vanguard, and threw the Wei into panic.

sentences.zh: 慶之還共諸將連營西進，據渦陽城，與魏相持，自春至冬，各數十百戰。

translations.literal: Qingzhi returned and with the other generals joined camps marching west, holding Guoyang city, in stalemate with Wei from spring to winter, dozens of battles each.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi rejoined the other generals, pushed west in linked camps, and held Guoyang. From spring through winter the two sides fought scores of battles.

sentences.zh: 師老氣衰，魏之援兵復欲築壘於軍後。

translations.literal: The troops were worn and their spirit decayed; Wei's relief force again intended to build ramparts behind the army.
translations.idiomatic: The army grew weary and morale sagged. Wei reinforcements began building fortifications behind the Liang lines.

sentences.zh: 仲宗等恐腹背受敵，謀退。

translations.literal: Congzong and the others feared attack from front and rear and planned to retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Congzong and the others, fearing attack from both sides, planned to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 慶之杖節軍門，曰：「須虜圍合，然後與戰；

translations.literal: Qingzhi, staff in hand at the army gate, said: "We must wait until the barbarians completely surround us, then we fight;
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi stood at the camp gate, tally in hand, and declared, "Wait until the enemy encircles us completely—then we fight;

sentences.zh: 若欲班師，慶之別有密敕。」

translations.literal: If you wish to withdraw, Qingzhi has a separate secret order.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone wants to retreat, I have a secret order that says otherwise.

sentences.zh: 仲宗壯其計，乃從之。

translations.literal: Congzong admired his plan and followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Congzong admired the plan and agreed.

sentences.zh: 魏人掎角作十三城，慶之陷其四壘。

translations.literal: The Wei men set up thirteen cities in pincer formation; Qingzhi captured four of the fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei built thirteen linked fortresses. Qingzhi took four of them.

sentences.zh: 九城兵甲猶盛，乃陳其俘馘，鼓噪攻之，遂奔潰，斬獲略盡，渦水咽流。

translations.literal: The other nine cities' arms were still strong; he displayed the captives and severed ears, attacking with battle cries; they fled in rout; slaughter and capture were nearly complete; the Wo River choked with corpses.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining nine still held strong garrisons. Qingzhi paraded prisoners and severed heads, attacked with a battle roar, and routed them. Slaughter and capture were nearly total; the Wo River ran choked with bodies.

sentences.zh: 詔以渦陽之地置西徐州。

translations.literal: An edict established Western Xuzhou on the land of Guoyang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict created Western Xuzhou on the conquered territory.

sentences.zh: 眾軍乘勝前頓城父。

translations.literal: The army pressed on in victory and encamped at Chengfu.
translations.idiomatic: The army pressed its advantage and encamped at Chengfu.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘉焉，手詔慰勉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was pleased and personally wrote an edict to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was delighted and sent a personal edict of praise and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 大通初，魏北海王元顥來降，武帝以慶之為假節、飆勇將軍，送顥還北。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai in Wei, came over to surrender; Emperor Wu appointed Qingzhi Acting Bearer of the Staff and Ferocious Courage General to escort Hao north.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Datong, Wei's Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, defected. The Emperor made Qingzhi Acting Bearer of the Staff and Ferocious Courage General and sent him north with Hao.

sentences.zh: 顥于渙水即魏帝號，授慶之前軍大都督。

translations.literal: Hao at the Huan River assumed the Wei imperial title and appointed Qingzhi Grand Commander of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: At the Huan River Hao declared himself Wei emperor and made Qingzhi Grand Commander of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 自銍縣進，遂至睢陽。

translations.literal: Advancing from Quan county, they reached Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Marching from Quan county, they reached Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 魏將丘大千有眾七萬，分築九壘以拒。

translations.literal: The Wei general Qiu Daqian had seventy thousand men and built nine fortresses in separate positions to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Wei general Qiu Daqian had seventy thousand men and built nine fortresses to block them.

sentences.zh: 慶之自旦至申，攻陷其三，大千乃降。

translations.literal: From dawn to mid-afternoon Qingzhi captured three of them; Daqian then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: From dawn to mid-afternoon Qingzhi took three of them. Daqian surrendered.

sentences.zh: 時魏濟陰王元暉業率羽林庶子二萬人來救梁、宋，進屯考城。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Yeye, Prince of Jiyin in Wei, led twenty thousand Guardians of the Forest and Commoners to save Liang and Song, advancing to encamp at Kaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Prince of Jiyin, Yuan Yeye, then marched with twenty thousand Guardians of the Forest to relieve Liang and Song, encamping at Kaocheng.

sentences.zh: 慶之攻陷其城，禽暉業，仍趣大梁。

translations.literal: Qingzhi captured the city, took Yeye prisoner, and pressed on to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi stormed the city, captured Yeye, and pressed on toward Daliang.

sentences.zh: 顥進慶之徐州刺史、武都郡王，仍率眾而西。

translations.literal: Hao promoted Qingzhi to Inspector of Xuzhou and Prince of Wudu, and still led the army west.
translations.idiomatic: Hao promoted Qingzhi to Inspector of Xuzhou and Prince of Wudu, then continued west at the head of the army.

sentences.zh: 魏左僕射楊昱等率禦仗羽林宗子庶子眾七萬據滎陽拒顥，兵強城固，魏將元天穆大軍復將至，先遣其驃騎將軍爾朱兆、騎將魯安等援楊昱，又遣右僕射爾朱世隆、西荊州刺史王羆據虎牢。

translations.literal: Yang Yu, Left Vice Minister of Wei, and others led seventy thousand Imperial Guards, Guardians of the Forest, Imperial Clansmen, and Commoners to hold Xingyang against Hao; the troops were strong and the walls solid; the Wei general Yuan Tianmu's great army was also about to arrive; he first sent his Biaoqi General Erzhu Zhao, cavalry general Lu An, and others to aid Yang Yu, and also sent Right Vice Minister Erzhu Shilong and Wang Pi, Inspector of Western Jing, to hold Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu, Wei's Left Vice Minister, held Xingyang with seventy thousand Imperial Guards and other troops. The garrison was strong and the walls solid. Yuan Tianmu's main army was approaching; he sent Erzhu Zhao and Lu An ahead to reinforce Yang Yu, and Erzhu Shilong and Wang Pi, Inspector of Western Jing, to hold Hulao.

sentences.zh: 時滎陽未拔，士眾皆恐。

translations.literal: Xingyang had not yet been taken; officers and soldiers were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyang had not fallen, and the men were afraid.

sentences.zh: 慶之乃解鞍秣馬，宣喻眾曰：「我等才有七千，賊眾四十餘萬。

translations.literal: Qingzhi thereupon un-saddled and fed the horses, and addressed the troops: "We have only seven thousand men; the enemy more than four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi had the horses unsaddled and fed, then addressed the troops: "We number only seven thousand. The enemy exceeds four hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，義不圖存，須平其城壘。」

translations.literal: In today's affair, in honor we cannot plan to survive; we must level their walls.
translations.idiomatic: Today honor forbids us to think of survival. We must take their walls.

sentences.zh: 一鼓悉使登城，壯士東陽宋景休、義興魚天湣踰堞而入，遂克之。

translations.literal: At the first drum all were made to mount the wall; the stalwarts Song Jingxiu of Dongyang and Yu Tianmin of Yixing climbed over the parapet and entered; they captured it.
translations.idiomatic: At the first drum he sent every man up the wall. Song Jingxiu of Dongyang and Yu Tianmin of Yixing scaled the parapet and broke in. The city fell.

sentences.zh: 俄而魏陣外合，慶之率精兵三千大破之。

translations.literal: Soon Wei forces joined outside; Qingzhi led three thousand elite troops and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Wei forces soon closed in from outside. Qingzhi led three thousand picked men and routed them.

sentences.zh: 魯安於陣乞降，天穆、兆單騎獲免。

translations.literal: Lu An begged to surrender on the field; Tianmu and Zhao escaped alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Lu An surrendered on the field. Tianmu and Zhao escaped alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 進赴虎牢，爾朱世隆棄城走。

translations.literal: Pressing on to Hulao, Erzhu Shilong abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi pressed on to Hulao. Erzhu Shilong abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 魏孝莊出居河北。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei went out to dwell north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei fled north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 其臨淮王彧、安豐王延明率百僚備法駕迎顥入洛陽宮，御前殿，改元大赦。

translations.literal: The Prince of Huaihai Yu and the Prince of Anfeng Yanming led all officials with imperial equipage to welcome Hao into Luoyang Palace; he ascended the front hall, changed the era name, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Huaihai and Anfeng, Yu and Yanming, led the officials with the imperial carriage to welcome Hao into Luoyang Palace. He took the front hall, changed the reign title, and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 顥以慶之為車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Hao made Qingzhi Cavalry Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Hao made Qingzhi Cavalry Grand General.

sentences.zh: 魏上党王元天穆又攻拔大梁，分遣王老生、費穆據虎牢，刁宣、刁雙入梁、宋，慶之隨方掩襲，並降，天穆與十餘騎北度河。

translations.literal: Yuan Tianmu, Prince of Shangdang in Wei, again captured Daliang and dispatched Wang Laosheng and Fei Mu to hold Hulao, and Diao Xuan and Diao Shuang to enter Liang and Song; Qingzhi attacked as the situation dictated; all surrendered; Tianmu with a dozen horsemen crossed north over the river.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, retook Daliang and sent Wang Laosheng and Fei Mu to hold Hulao and Diao Xuan and Diao Shuang into Liang and Song. Qingzhi struck wherever opportunity offered; all surrendered. Tianmu crossed the river north with a dozen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 慶之麾下悉著白袍，所向披靡。

translations.literal: All under Qingzhi's command wore white robes; wherever they went, none could stand before them.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi's men all wore white robes and swept aside everything in their path.

sentences.zh: 先是洛中謠曰：「名軍大將莫自牢，千兵萬馬避白袍。」

translations.literal: Before this a song in Luoyang said: "Famous generals, do not rely on yourselves alone; ten thousand soldiers and horses flee the white robes.
translations.idiomatic: A Luoyang ballad had already warned: "Famous generals, don't trust your walls—ten thousand horsemen flee the white robes.

sentences.zh: 自發銍縣至洛陽，十四旬平三十二城，四十七戰，所向無前。

translations.literal: From setting out from Quan county to Luoyang, in fourteen ten-day periods he pacified thirty-two cities and fought forty-seven battles; wherever he went, none could stand before him.
translations.idiomatic: From Quan county to Luoyang, in fourteen ten-day periods he took thirty-two cities in forty-seven battles. Nothing stood before him.

sentences.zh: 初，魏莊帝單騎度河，宮衛嬪侍無改于常。

translations.literal: Initially Emperor Zhuang of Wei alone on horseback crossed the river; palace guards and attendants were unchanged as usual.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang of Wei fled alone on horseback across the river, his palace guards and attendants carried on as if nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 顥既得志，荒於酒色，不復視事，與安豐、臨淮計將背梁，以時事未安，且資慶之力用。

translations.literal: Hao having gotten his wish, debauched himself in wine and women and no longer attended to affairs; with Anfeng and Huaihai he plotted to turn against Liang; as affairs were not yet settled, for the time being he relied on Qingzhi's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hao had what he wanted, he sank into wine and women and neglected affairs. With the Princes of Anfeng and Huaihai he plotted to betray Liang, but while the situation remained unsettled he still relied on Qingzhi's strength.

sentences.zh: 慶之心知之，乃說顥曰：「今遠來至此，未伏尚多，宜啟天子，更請精兵；

translations.literal: Qingzhi knew it in his heart; he urged Hao: "Having come far to this place, many still remain unsubdued; you should memorialize the Son of Heaven and request more elite troops;
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi saw through it. He urged Hao, "Many here still hold out. You should petition the Son of Heaven for more elite troops;

sentences.zh: 並勒諸州有南人沒此者，悉須部送。」

translations.literal: Also instruct all provinces that southerners captured here must all be dispatched."
translations.idiomatic: and order every province to send up all southerners held captive here."

sentences.zh: 顥欲從之，元延明說顥曰：「慶之兵不出數千，已自難制，今更增其眾，寧肯為用？

translations.literal: Hao wished to follow this; Yuan Yanming persuaded Hao: "Qingzhi's troops number only a few thousand and are already hard to control; now if you increase his forces, will he willingly serve?
translations.idiomatic: Hao was inclined to agree, but Yuan Yanming warned him, "Qingzhi commands only a few thousand men and is already hard to control. Send him more troops—will he still obey?

sentences.zh: 魏之宗社，於斯而滅。」

translations.literal: Wei's ancestral shrine—at this it perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's dynasty would be finished.

sentences.zh: 顥由是疑慶之，乃密啟武帝停軍。

translations.literal: Hao therefore suspected Qingzhi and secretly memorialized Emperor Wu to halt reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Hao grew suspicious and secretly asked Emperor Wu to halt reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 洛下南人不出一萬，魏人十倍。

translations.literal: Southerners in Luoyang numbered not even ten thousand; Wei men were ten times as many.
translations.idiomatic: Southerners in Luoyang numbered fewer than ten thousand; the Wei outnumbered them ten to one.

sentences.zh: 軍副馬佛念言于慶之曰：「勳高不賞，震主身危，二事既有，將軍豈得無慮？

translations.literal: The deputy Ma Fonian said to Qingzhi: "Merit high and unrewarded, the lord's majesty fears the body—these two things being present, how can the general not worry?
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Ma Fonian said to Qingzhi, "Great merit goes unrewarded, and power that awes the throne endangers its holder. With both in play, can you afford not to worry?

sentences.zh: 今將軍威震中原，聲動河塞，屠顥據洛，則千載一時。」

translations.literal: Now the general's prestige shakes the Central Plain and his fame moves the Yellow River frontier; kill Hao and hold Luoyang—then once in a millennium.
translations.idiomatic: Your prestige now shakes the Central Plain and your name resounds to the Yellow River frontier. Kill Hao and hold Luoyang—a chance that comes once in an age.

sentences.zh: 慶之不從。

translations.literal: Qingzhi did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi refused.

sentences.zh: 顥前以慶之為徐州刺史，因求之鎮，顥心憚之，遂不遣。

translations.literal: Hao had earlier made Qingzhi Inspector of Xuzhou; Qingzhi requested to garrison there; Hao feared him in his heart and therefore did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had earlier made Qingzhi Inspector of Xuzhou. When Qingzhi asked to take up the post, Hao, fearing him, refused.

sentences.zh: 魏將爾朱榮、爾朱世隆、元天穆、爾朱兆等眾號百萬，挾魏帝來攻顥。

translations.literal: The Wei generals Erzhu Rong, Erzhu Shilong, Yuan Tianmu, Erzhu Zhao, and others claimed a million men and brought the Wei emperor to attack Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei generals Erzhu Rong, Erzhu Shilong, Yuan Tianmu, and Erzhu Zhao marched with what they claimed was a million men and the Wei emperor to attack Hao.

sentences.zh: 顥據洛陽六十五日，凡所得城一時歸魏，慶之度河守北中郎城。

translations.literal: Hao held Luoyang for sixty-five days; all cities taken at once returned to Wei; Qingzhi crossed the river to hold North Central Gentleman city.
translations.idiomatic: Hao held Luoyang for sixty-five days. Every city he had taken reverted to Wei at once. Qingzhi crossed the river and held North Central Gentleman City.

sentences.zh: 三日十一戰，傷殺甚眾。

translations.literal: In three days eleven battles; many wounded and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In three days he fought eleven battles. Casualties were heavy on both sides.

sentences.zh: 榮將退還，時有善天文人劉靈助謂榮曰：「不出十日，河南大定。」

translations.literal: Rong was about to retreat; at that time the skilled astronomer Liu Lingzhu told Rong: "Within ten days Henan will be greatly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was about to withdraw when the astrologer Liu Lingzhu told him, "Within ten days Henan will be secured.

sentences.zh: 榮乃為伐濟自硤石，與顥戰於河橋。

translations.literal: Rong therefore opened a route at Xiaoxi from Xiashi and fought Hao at River Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Rong cut a path through the Xiaoxi ford at Xiashi and met Hao at River Bridge.

sentences.zh: 顥大敗，走至臨潁被禽，洛陽復入魏。

translations.literal: Hao was greatly defeated; he fled to Linying and was captured; Luoyang again entered Wei control.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was routed, fled to Linying, and was captured. Luoyang returned to Wei.

sentences.zh: 慶之馬步數千結陣東反，榮親自來追，軍人死散。

translations.literal: Qingzhi's several thousand infantry and cavalry formed ranks and turned east; Rong personally came in pursuit; soldiers died and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi formed his few thousand horse and foot and turned east. Rong pursued in person. His men were killed or scattered.

sentences.zh: 慶之乃落鬚髮為沙門，間行至豫州，州人程道雍等潛送出汝陰。

translations.literal: Qingzhi thereupon cut off his beard and hair to become a monk; by hidden paths he reached Yuzhou; the provincials Cheng Daoyong and others secretly escorted him out via Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi shaved his head and beard and went as a monk by back roads to Yuzhou, where Cheng Daoyong and others smuggled him out through Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 至都，仍以功除右衛將軍，封永興侯。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, he was still for merit made Right Guard General and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the capital he was made Right Guard General and Marquis of Yongxing for his service.

sentences.zh: 出為北兗州刺史、都督緣淮諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Inspector of Northern Yanzhou and Commander of all military affairs along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Inspector of Northern Yanzhou and commander of forces along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 會有祅賊沙門僧強自稱為帝，土豪蔡伯寵起兵應之，攻陷北徐州。

translations.literal: It happened that the sorcerer monk Seng Qiang styled himself emperor; the local magnate Cai Bochong raised troops in response and captured Northern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A sorcerer monk, Seng Qiang, declared himself emperor. The local strongman Cai Bochong rose in support and seized Northern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔慶之討焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qingzhi to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Qingzhi to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 慶之斬伯寵、僧強，傳其首。

translations.literal: Qingzhi beheaded Bochong and Seng Qiang and sent their heads.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi beheaded Bochong and Seng Qiang and sent their heads to the capital.

sentences.zh: 中大通二年，除南北司二州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong, he was made Inspector of both Southern and Northern Si provinces, with the added title of Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was made Inspector of both Southern and Northern Si provinces and given overall command.

sentences.zh: 慶之至鎮，遂圍縣瓠，破魏潁州刺史婁起、揚州刺史是雲寶于溱水。

translations.literal: When Qingzhi reached his post, he besieged Xiangcheng and defeated Lou Qi, Inspector of Yingzhou in Wei, and Shi Yunbao, Inspector of Yangzhou, at the Zhen River.
translations.idiomatic: At his post Qingzhi besieged Xiangcheng and defeated Wei's Inspectors of Ying and Yang, Lou Qi and Shi Yunbao, at the Zhen River.

sentences.zh: 又破行台孫騰、豫州刺史堯雄、梁州刺史司馬恭于楚城。

translations.literal: He also defeated Sun Teng of the Mobile Command, Yao Xiong, Inspector of Yuzhou, and Sima Gong, Inspector of Liangzhou, at Chucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated Sun Teng of the Mobile Command and Wei's Inspectors Yao Xiong of Yuzhou and Sima Gong of Liangzhou at Chucheng.

sentences.zh: 罷義陽鎮兵，停水陸轉運，江湘諸州並得休息。

translations.literal: He dismissed the Yiyang garrison troops and stopped water and land transport; the Jiang and Xiang provinces all obtained rest.
translations.idiomatic: He disbanded the Yiyang garrison and halted water and land transport, giving the Jiang and Xiang provinces relief from the burden.

sentences.zh: 開田六千頃，二年之後，倉廩充實。

translations.literal: He opened fields of six thousand qing; after two years the granaries were full.
translations.idiomatic: He opened six thousand qing of fields; within two years the granaries were full.

sentences.zh: 又表省南司州，復安陸郡，置上明郡。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to abolish Southern Si province, restore Anlu commandery, and establish Shangming commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to abolish Southern Si province, restore Anlu commandery, and create Shangming commandery.

sentences.zh: 大同二年，魏遣將侯景攻下楚州，執刺史桓和。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong, Wei sent the general Hou Jing to capture Chuzhou and took Inspector Huan He prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong, Wei sent Hou Jing to take Chuzhou and captured Inspector Huan He.

sentences.zh: 景仍進軍淮上，慶之破之。

translations.literal: Jing still advanced his army on the Huai; Qingzhi defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing pressed on toward the Huai. Qingzhi defeated him.

sentences.zh: 時大寒雪，景棄輜重走。

translations.literal: At the time there was extreme cold and snow; Jing abandoned his baggage and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In bitter cold and snow Jing abandoned his baggage train and fled.

sentences.zh: 是歲豫州饑，慶之開倉振給，多所全濟。

translations.literal: That year Yuzhou had famine; Qingzhi opened the granaries to relieve and supply; many were fully saved.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yuzhou suffered famine. Qingzhi opened the granaries and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 州人李升等八百人表求樹碑頌德，詔許焉。

translations.literal: Eight hundred provincials including Li Sheng memorialized requesting a stele to praise his virtue; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Eight hundred locals led by Li Sheng petitioned for a stele in his honor. The court approved.

sentences.zh: 五年卒，諡曰武。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died; his posthumous title was Wu (Martial).
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of the reign and was posthumously titled Martial.

sentences.zh: 慶之性祗慎，每奉詔敕，必洗沐拜受。

translations.literal: Qingzhi's nature was reverent and cautious; every time he received an edict he would wash and bathe before accepting it with a bow.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi was reverent and careful. Whenever an edict arrived he washed and bowed before accepting it.

sentences.zh: 儉素不衣紈綺，不好絲竹。

translations.literal: Frugal and plain, he did not wear silk brocade and did not love music.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly, wore no silk, and cared nothing for music.

sentences.zh: 射不穿劄，馬非所便，而善撫軍士，能得其死力。

translations.literal: His archery could not pierce a leaf; horses were not his forte; yet he was good at soothing soldiers and could obtain their death-effort.
translations.idiomatic: He could not shoot an arrow through a leaf and was no horseman, yet he knew how to win soldiers' hearts and call forth their utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 長子昭嗣。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zhaosi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zhaosi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 梁世寒門達者唯慶之與俞藥，藥初為武帝左右，帝謂曰：「俞氏無先賢，世人云'俞錢'，非君子所宜，改姓喻。」

translations.literal: In the Liang dynasty those of humble gates who rose to eminence were only Qingzhi and Yu Yao; Yao was initially at Emperor Wu's side; the Emperor said: "The Yu clan has no ancient worthies; people say 'Yu money'—not what a gentleman should bear; change your surname to Yu (meaning 'to illustrate').
translations.idiomatic: In Liang times only Qingzhi and Yu Yao rose from humble origins. Yao had served at the Emperor's side. The Emperor told him, "Your clan has no distinguished ancestors. People mock the name as 'Yu money'—unfit for a gentleman. Change it to Yu, 'to illustrate.'

sentences.zh: 藥曰：「當令姓自於臣。」

translations.literal: Yao said: "Let the surname reflect on the subject."
translations.idiomatic: Yao replied, "Let the surname speak for the man himself."

sentences.zh: 歷位雲旗將軍，安州刺史。

translations.literal: He passed through offices to General of Cloud Banners and Inspector of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of Cloud Banners and Inspector of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 慶之第五子昕字君章，七歲能騎射。

translations.literal: Qingzhi's fifth son Xin, styled Junzhang, at seven could ride and shoot.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi's fifth son Xin, courtesy name Junzhang, could ride and shoot by age seven.

sentences.zh: 十二隨父入洛，遇疾還都，詣鴻臚卿朱異。

translations.literal: At twelve he followed his father into Luoyang; he met illness and returned to the capital; he visited Zhu Yi, Chamberlain for Dependent States.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he followed his father to Luoyang. Illness sent him back to the capital, where he called on Zhu Yi, Chamberlain for Dependent States.

sentences.zh: 異訪北間事，昕聚土畫城，指麾分別，異甚奇之。

translations.literal: Yi inquired about northern affairs; Xin piled earth to draw a city, directing and distinguishing positions; Yi greatly marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Yi questioned him about the north. Xin molded earth into a map of the cities and traced the deployments. Yi was astonished.

sentences.zh: 慶之在縣瓠，魏驍將堯雄子寶樂特為敢勇，求單騎校戰，昕躍馬直趣寶樂，雄即潰散。

translations.literal: When Qingzhi was at Xiangcheng, Baoyue, son of Wei's fierce general Yao Xiong, was specially daring and brave; he requested single combat on horseback; Xin leaped on his horse and charged straight at Baoyue; Xiong immediately routed and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangcheng, Yao Xiong's son Baoyue, a Wei champion, challenged anyone to single combat. Xin spurred straight at him. Yao Xiong's force broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 後為臨川太守。

translations.literal: Later he was made Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He later became prefect of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，侯景圍曆陽，敕召昕還。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged Liyang; an edict summoned Xin back.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged Liyang. An edict recalled Xin.

sentences.zh: 昕啟云：「採石急須重鎮，王質水軍輕弱，恐虜必濟。」

translations.literal: Xin memorialized: "Caishi urgently needs a strong garrison; Wang Zhi's naval forces are light and weak—I fear the enemy will surely cross.
translations.idiomatic: Xin memorialized, "Caishi needs a strong garrison at once. Wang Zhi's fleet is too weak—the enemy will surely cross.

sentences.zh: 乃板昕為雲騎將軍代質，未及下渚，景已度江，為景所禽。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xin was appointed on the fly as General of Cloud Cavalry to replace Zhi; before reaching the lower ford, Jing had already crossed the river; Xin was captured by Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was hurriedly appointed General of Cloud Cavalry to replace Wang Zhi. Before he reached the lower ford, Jing had already crossed the Yangtze and captured him.

sentences.zh: 令收集部曲將用之，昕誓而不許。

translations.literal: Jing ordered him to gather his troops for use; Xin swore an oath and would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Jing ordered him to rally his followers for service. Xin swore he would not.

sentences.zh: 景使其儀同範桃棒嚴禁之，昕因說桃棒令率所領歸降，襲殺王偉、宋子仙。

translations.literal: Jing had his Ceremonial Companion Fan Taobang strictly guard him; Xin thereupon persuaded Taobang to lead his subordinates to surrender and return, and assassinate Wang Wei and Song Zixian.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had Fan Taobang guard him closely. Xin persuaded Taobang to defect with his men and kill Wang Wei and Song Zixian.

sentences.zh: 桃棒許之。

translations.literal: Taobang consented.
translations.idiomatic: Taobang agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂立盟射城中，遣昕夜縋而入。

translations.literal: Thereupon they established the alliance by shooting an arrow into the city, and sent Xin down by rope at night to enter.
translations.idiomatic: They sealed the pact by shooting an arrow into the city and sent Xin in by rope that night.

sentences.zh: 武帝大喜，敕即受降。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was greatly pleased and ordered that the surrender be accepted at once.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was overjoyed and ordered the surrender accepted immediately.

sentences.zh: 簡文遲疑，累日不決。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen hesitated; for many days he could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen wavered, and for days could not decide.

sentences.zh: 外事泄，昕弗之知，猶依期而下。

translations.literal: The outside affair was leaked; Xin did not know of it and still descended according to schedule.
translations.idiomatic: The plan leaked, but Xin knew nothing and came down on schedule.

sentences.zh: 景邀得之，逼昕令更射書城中，云：「桃棒且輕將數十人先入」。

translations.literal: Jing intercepted and captured him, forcing Xin to shoot another letter into the city saying: "Taobang will first lead several dozen light troops to enter."
translations.idiomatic: Jing caught him and forced him to shoot another message into the city: "Taobang will enter first with a few dozen light troops."

sentences.zh: 景欲裹甲隨之。

translations.literal: Jing wished to don armor and follow.
translations.idiomatic: Jing planned to follow in armor.

sentences.zh: 昕不從，遂見害。

translations.literal: Xin did not comply and was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xin refused and was killed.

sentences.zh: 少弟 暄

translations.literal: Younger brother Xuan
translations.idiomatic: The Younger Brother: Xuan

sentences.zh: 少弟暄，學不師受，文才俊逸。

translations.literal: The younger brother Xuan studied without taking teachers; his literary talent was brilliant and unfettered.
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother Xuan was self-taught, with a brilliant literary gift.

sentences.zh: 尤嗜酒，無節操，遍曆王公門，沈湎喧譊，過差非度。

translations.literal: He especially loved wine, had no restraint, visited every prince and duke's gate, drowned in drink with clamor, exceeding all bounds.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to wine, without restraint, and haunted the houses of princes and dukes, drinking himself into uproar far beyond all propriety.

sentences.zh: 其兄子秀常憂之，致書于暄友人何胥，冀以諷諫。

translations.literal: His nephew Xiu often worried about him and sent a letter to Xuan's friend He Xu, hoping to admonish him indirectly.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Xiu worried constantly and wrote to Xuan's friend He Xu, hoping he might offer a tactful warning.

sentences.zh: 暄聞之，與秀書曰：

translations.literal: When Xuan heard of it, he wrote to Xiu, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan heard, he wrote back to Xiu:

sentences.zh: 旦見汝書與孝典，陳吾飲酒過差。

translations.literal: This morning I saw your letter to Xiaodian, stating that my drinking exceeds all bounds.
translations.idiomatic: This morning I saw your letter to Xiaodian complaining that I drink too much.

sentences.zh: 吾有此好五十餘年，昔吳國張長公亦稱耽嗜，吾見張時，伊已六十，自言引滿大勝少年時。

translations.literal: I have had this fondness for more than fifty years. Formerly Zhang the Elder of Wu state was also said to be addicted to drink; when I saw Zhang he was already sixty and said himself that filling his cup surpassed his youth.
translations.idiomatic: I have loved wine for more than fifty years. Zhang the Elder of Wu was a famous drinker too. When I met him at sixty, he said he could hold his liquor better than in his youth.

sentences.zh: 吾今所進亦多於往日。

translations.literal: What I consume now is also more than in former days.
translations.idiomatic: I drink even more now than I did then.

sentences.zh: 老而彌篤，唯吾與張季舒耳。

translations.literal: Growing old I become only more devoted—this is true of me and Zhang Jishu alone.
translations.idiomatic: Age has only deepened the habit—Zhang Jishu and I alone know what that means.

sentences.zh: 吾方與此子交歡於地下，汝欲夭吾所志邪？

translations.literal: I am just about to enjoy fellowship with this man underground—do you wish to cut short my aspiration?
translations.idiomatic: I am about to drink with that man in the world below. Do you mean to cut short my chosen path?

sentences.zh: 昔阮咸、阮籍同游竹林，宣子不聞斯言。

translations.literal: Formerly Ruan Xian and Ruan Ji roamed the bamboo grove together; Xuanzi never heard such talk.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xian and Ruan Ji once roamed the Bamboo Grove together. Would Xuanzi have spoken as you do?

sentences.zh: 王湛能玄言巧騎，武子呼為癡叔。

translations.literal: Wang Zhan could discourse on the abstruse and ride skillfully; Wuzi called him the Idiot Uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan could speak abstruse philosophy and ride superbly, yet Wuzi called him the Idiot Uncle.

sentences.zh: 何陳留之風不嗣，太原之氣巋然，翻成可怪！

translations.literal: Why has the spirit of Chenliu not continued, while the air of Taiyuan stands firm—this instead becomes strange!
translations.idiomatic: Why has the free spirit of Chenliu died out while the stolid air of Taiyuan endures? That is what is truly strange!

sentences.zh: 吾既寂漠當世，朽病殘年，產不異于顏原，名未動於卿相，若不日飲醇酒，復欲安歸？

translations.literal: I am already obscure in this age, a decayed invalid in my remaining years; my estate is no different from Yan Hui or Yuan Xian, my name has not moved ministers and chancellors—if I do not daily drink fine wine, where else shall I turn?
translations.idiomatic: I am forgotten in this world, broken and old. My means are those of Yan Hui or Yuan Xian; my name has never reached the great ministers. If I do not drink good wine every day, where else is there for me to go?

sentences.zh: 汝以飲酒為非，吾以不飲酒為過。

translations.literal: You take drinking as wrong; I take not drinking as fault.
translations.idiomatic: You call drinking a fault; I call sobriety the fault.

sentences.zh: 昔周伯仁度江唯三日醒，吾不以為少；

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou Borren crossed the river sober only three days—I do not consider that too little;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Borren crossed the Yangtze he was sober only three days in all—I do not call that too little;

sentences.zh: 鄭康成一飲三百杯，吾不以為多。

translations.literal: Zheng Kangcheng once drank three hundred cups in a sitting—I do not consider that too much.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Kangcheng drank three hundred cups at one sitting—I do not call that too much.

sentences.zh: 然洪醉之後，有得有失。

translations.literal: Yet after deep drunkenness there are gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet deep drunkenness has its gains and its losses.

sentences.zh: 成塚養之志，是其得也；

translations.literal: Fulfilling the ambition to raise a mound for one's parents—that is its gain;
translations.idiomatic: Fulfilling the filial duty of raising a family tomb—that is the gain;

sentences.zh: 使次公之狂，是其失也。

translations.literal: Producing the madness of Cigong—that is its loss.
translations.idiomatic: Producing the wildness of Cigong—that is the loss.

sentences.zh: 吾常譬酒之猶水，亦可以濟舟，亦可以覆舟。

translations.literal: I often compare wine to water: it can also ferry a boat, and it can also capsize a boat.
translations.idiomatic: I often compare wine to water—it can carry a boat or sink one.

sentences.zh: 故江諮議有言：「酒猶兵也。

translations.literal: Therefore Adviser Jiang said: "Wine is like arms.
translations.idiomatic: Adviser Jiang once said, "Wine is like arms.

sentences.zh: 兵可千日而不用，不可一日而不備。

translations.literal: Arms may go a thousand days unused, but cannot go a single day unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Arms may lie unused for a thousand days, but you cannot leave them unready for a single day.

sentences.zh: 酒可千日而不飲，不可一飲而不醉。」

translations.literal: Wine may go a thousand days undrunk, but one cannot drink once without becoming drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Wine may go undrunk for a thousand days, but once you drink you must be drunk.

sentences.zh: 美哉江公，可與共論酒矣。

translations.literal: How fine is Lord Jiang—one could discuss wine with him!
translations.idiomatic: Splendid Lord Jiang—he was a man to discuss wine with!

sentences.zh: 汝驚吾墯馬侍中之門，陷池武陵之第，遍佈朝野，自言焦悚。

translations.literal: You are alarmed that I fell from my horse at the Attendant-in-Ordinary's gate and fell into the pool at the Prince of Wuling's mansion—news spread through court and countryside, and I call myself anxious and ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: You fuss over my fall from a horse at the Attendant-in-Ordinary's gate and my plunge into the pool at Prince Wuling's mansion—news spread everywhere, and I admit I was mortified.

sentences.zh: 「丘也幸，苟有過，人必知之」。

translations.literal: "Qiu is fortunate: if there is fault, people are sure to know it."
translations.idiomatic: As Confucius said, "If I err, people are sure to know."

sentences.zh: 吾生平所願，身沒之後，題吾墓云：「陳故酒徒陳君之神道」。

translations.literal: My lifelong wish is that after my death my tomb be inscribed: "Spirit Way of Lord Chen, former wine-bibber of Chen."
translations.idiomatic: All my life I have wished that after death my tomb would read: "Spirit Way of Lord Chen, Wine-Drinker of Chen."

sentences.zh: 若斯志意，豈避南征之不復，賈誼之慟哭者哉。

translations.literal: With such aspiration and intent, how would I shrink from never returning from the southern expedition, or from Jia Yi's wailing grief?
translations.idiomatic: With such an ambition, would I fear never returning from the south, or weep like Jia Yi?

sentences.zh: 何水曹眼不識杯鐺，吾口不離瓢杓，汝甯與何同日而醒，與吾同日而醉乎？

translations.literal: He the Water Bureau's eyes do not know cup and ladle; my mouth never leaves gourd dipper and ladle—would you rather wake on the same day as He, or get drunk on the same day as me?
translations.idiomatic: He of the Water Bureau cannot tell one cup from another; my lips never leave the ladle. Would you rather wake sober with He, or get drunk with me?

sentences.zh: 政言其醒可及，其醉不可及也。

translations.literal: This is precisely to say that his sobriety can be matched, but his drunkenness cannot be reached.
translations.idiomatic: I mean only that you might match him sober—you could never match me drunk.

sentences.zh: 速營糟丘，吾將老焉。

translations.literal: Quickly build the Wine Mound—I shall grow old there.
translations.idiomatic: Build me a hill of mash—I mean to grow old upon it.

sentences.zh: 爾無多言，非爾所及。

translations.literal: You, say no more—it is not within your reach.
translations.idiomatic: Say no more. This is beyond you.

sentences.zh: 暄以落魄不為中正所品，久不得調。

translations.literal: Because of his dissolute ways Xuan was not rated by the Rectifier and for a long time could not obtain appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's dissolute life kept the Rectifier from rating him, and for years he received no appointment.

sentences.zh: 陳天康中，徐陵為吏部尚書，精簡人物，縉紳之士皆向慕焉。

translations.literal: In the Tiankang era of Chen, Xu Ling was Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, refining and selecting men of talent; gentry and officials all looked up to him with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: During Chen's Tiankang era, Xu Ling was Minister of Personnel and renowned for judging talent. Officials and gentry alike admired him.

sentences.zh: 暄以玉帽簪插髻，紅絲布裹頭，袍拂踝，靴至膝，不陳爵裏，直上陵坐。

translations.literal: Xuan wore a jade cap-pin stuck in his topknot, a red silk cloth wrapped around his head, a robe brushing his ankles, boots reaching his knees; without stating his rank and origin, he went straight up and sat before Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan appeared with a jade pin in his topknot, a red silk head-wrap, a robe sweeping his ankles, and boots to the knee. Without giving name or rank he walked in and sat down before Xu Ling.

sentences.zh: 陵不之識，命吏持下。

translations.literal: Ling did not recognize him and ordered an clerk to take him down.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling did not recognize him and ordered his clerks to remove him.

sentences.zh: 暄徐步而出，舉止自若，竟無怍容。

translations.literal: Xuan walked out slowly, his bearing composed, showing no shame at all.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan walked out slowly, perfectly at ease, without a trace of embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 作書謗陵，陵甚病之。

translations.literal: He wrote a letter slandering Ling; Ling was greatly vexed by it.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a letter mocking Xu Ling, who was deeply offended.

sentences.zh: 蘭欽字休明，中昌魏人也。

translations.literal: Lan Qin, styled Xiuming, was a native of Zhongchangwei.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Qin, courtesy name Xiuming, was from Zhongchangwei.

sentences.zh: 幼而果決，趫捷過人。

translations.literal: From youth he was resolute and decisive, swift and agile beyond others.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was bold and decisive, quicker and nimbler than other men.

sentences.zh: 宋末隨父子雲在洛陽，恒於市騎橐駝。

translations.literal: At the end of Song he followed his father Ziyun in Luoyang and constantly rode camels in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Song he followed his father Ziyun to Luoyang, where he often rode camels in the market.

sentences.zh: 後子雲還南，梁天監中以軍功至冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Later Ziyun returned south; in the Tianjian era of Liang, through military achievement he rose to Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyun later returned south, Lan Qin rose through battle honors in Liang's Tianjian era to Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 欽兼文德主帥，征南中五郡諸洞反者，所至皆平。

translations.literal: Qin also served as Commander of Wende and campaigned against the rebel cave-dwellers of the five southern commanderies; wherever he went all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: As Commander of Wende he campaigned against rebel cave tribes in five southern commanderies and pacified every place he reached.

sentences.zh: 欽有謀略，勇決善戰，步行日二百里，勇武過人。

translations.literal: Qin had stratagem and plan, was brave, resolute, and skilled in battle; on foot he could cover two hundred li in a day; his courage and martial prowess surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Qin was shrewd, bold, and a skilled fighter. On foot he could cover two hundred li in a day. His courage outmatched other men.

sentences.zh: 善撫馭，得人死力。

translations.literal: He was good at soothing and controlling men and could obtain their death-effort.
translations.idiomatic: He knew how to win men and call forth their utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 以軍功封安懷縣男。

translations.literal: Through military achievement he was enfeoffed as Baron of Anhuai county.
translations.idiomatic: For his military service he was enfeoffed as Baron of Anhuai.

sentences.zh: 累遷都督、梁南秦二州刺史，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to Commander and Inspector of both Liang and Nanchin provinces, and advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Commander and Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin, and was promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 征梁、漢，事平，進號智武將軍。

translations.literal: Campaigning in Liang and Han, when affairs were pacified he was advanced in title to Wise Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liang and Han campaign he was promoted to Wise Martial General.

sentences.zh: 改授都督、衡州刺史。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Commander and Inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Commander and Inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 未及述職，會西魏攻圍南鄭，梁州刺史杜懷寶來請救，欽乃大破魏軍，追入斜穀，斬獲略盡。

translations.literal: Before he could take up his duties, it happened that Western Wei attacked and besieged Nanzheng; Du Huaibao, Inspector of Liangzhou, came to request relief; Qin thereupon routed the Wei army greatly, pursued into Xie Valley, and slaughter and capture were nearly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up his post, Western Wei besieged Nanzheng. Liang Inspector Du Huaibao appealed for help. Qin routed the Wei army and pursued them into Xie Valley, slaughtering and capturing nearly all.

sentences.zh: 魏相安定公遣致馬二千疋，請結鄰好。

translations.literal: The Wei Chancellor the Duke of Anding sent two thousand horses as a gift and requested friendly relations as neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Chancellor, the Duke of Anding, sent two thousand horses and sought peace between neighbors.

sentences.zh: 欽百日之中再破魏軍，威振鄰國。

translations.literal: Within a hundred days Qin twice routed the Wei army; his prestige shook neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: Within a hundred days Qin defeated the Wei twice. His fame shook the neighboring states.

sentences.zh: 詔加散騎常侍，仍令述職。

translations.literal: An edict added the title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and still ordered him to take up his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and ordered to proceed to his post.

sentences.zh: 經廣州，因破俚帥陳文徹兄弟，並禽之。

translations.literal: Passing through Guangzhou, he thereupon defeated the Li chieftain Chen Wenche and his brothers and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Guangzhou he defeated the Li chieftain Chen Wenche and his brothers and took them captive.

sentences.zh: 至衡州，進號平南將軍，改封曲江縣公。

translations.literal: When he reached Hengzhou he was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the South and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Qujiang county.
