translations.idiomatic: At Hengzhou he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South and made Duke of Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 在州有惠政，吏人詣闕請立碑頌德，詔許焉。

translations.literal: In the province he had benevolent administration; officials and people went to the court requesting a stele to praise his virtue; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: His rule in the province was benevolent. Officials and people petitioned the court for a stele in his honor, and the edict approved.

sentences.zh: 後為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he became Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 前刺史新渝侯映之薨，南安侯恬權行州事，冀得即真。

translations.literal: The former Inspector the Marquis of Xinyu Yingzhi died; the Marquis of Nan'an Tian acted in the province's affairs by temporary authority, hoping to obtain the actual appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When the former inspector, the Marquis of Xinyu, died, the Marquis of Nan'an, Tian, acted as interim governor, hoping to keep the post.

sentences.zh: 及聞欽至嶺，原貨廚人，塗刀以毒，削瓜進之，欽及愛妾俱死。

translations.literal: When he heard Qin had reached the Ling range, he bribed the kitchen staff, smeared a knife with poison, sliced melon and presented it; Qin and his beloved concubine both died.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned Qin had crossed the Ling Pass, he bribed the kitchen staff, poisoned a knife, and served sliced melon. Qin and his favorite concubine both died.

sentences.zh: 帝聞大怒，檻車收恬，削爵土。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard he was greatly angered, had Tian taken in a caged cart, and stripped his title and fief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, furious, had Tian taken away in a prison cart and stripped of his title and fief.

sentences.zh: 欽子夏禮，侯景至曆陽，率其部曲邀景，兵敗死之。

translations.literal: Qin's son Xiali, when Hou Jing reached Liyang, led his personal troops to intercept Jing; the army was defeated and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's son Xiali, when Hou Jing reached Liyang, led his followers to intercept him, was defeated, and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：陳伯之雖輕狡為心，而勇勁自立，其累至爵位，蓋有由焉。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Although Chen Bozhi's heart was frivolous and cunning, he stood on his own through courage and vigor; that he accumulated rank to enfeoffment surely had its reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Chen Bozhi was frivolous and cunning at heart, yet he made his own way through courage and force. That he rose to enfeoffment was not without cause.

sentences.zh: 及喪亂既平，去就不已，卒得其死，亦為幸哉。

translations.literal: When the turmoil of loss and disorder was already pacified, his going and staying did not cease; that he finally obtained his death was also fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: After the chaos ended he wavered between loyalty and defection, yet died in his bed—a kind of fortune in itself.

sentences.zh: 慶之初同燕雀之遊，終懷鴻鵠之志，及乎一見任委，長驅伊、洛。

translations.literal: Qingzhi at first wandered like sparrows and finches, yet in the end harbored the wild swan's aspiration; once he was seen and entrusted, he drove far through Yi and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi began among the sparrows yet always nursed the wild swan's ambition. Once trusted with command, he swept through the Yi and Luo valleys.

sentences.zh: 前無強陣，攻靡堅城，雖南風不競，晚致傾覆，其所克捷，亦足稱之。

translations.literal: Before him no strong formation stood; no solid city he attacked withstood him; although the southern wind did not prevail and he ultimately met overturn late, what he captured and achieved is also enough to be praised.
translations.idiomatic: No enemy line held before him; no walled city withstood his assault. Though fortune turned against him in the end, what he conquered remains worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 蘭欽戰有先鳴，位非虛受，終逢鴆毒，唯命也夫。

translations.literal: Lan Qin in battle had the first cry of victory; his rank was not received in vain; that he finally met poisoned wine—such was fate.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Qin was always first in battle and earned every rank he held. That he died by poison was simply fate.
